Ben / Karthik —

Thanks — ran the numbers against our latency/throughput models. Summary and recommended plan below (TL;DR at top).

TL;DR: Recommend a 3-node Dedicated pool sized to 4x A100-80GB equiv per node (total 12x A100 equiv) in initial commit (Target). Conservative = 16x A100 equiv total (extra headroom), Aggressive = 8x total (cost-optimized, relies on >50% cache hit).

Assumptions and calculations:
- 220 qps sustained peak; avg request token cost estimated at 240 tokens.
- With Redwood batching and KV prefix caching we model ~35% effective token reduction for repeated prompts.
- Per-node throughput (A100-equivalent) measured in our benchmarks: ~100 qps sustained for mixed chat+embed workload under 95th percentile latency target.
- So 3 nodes x 100 qps = 300 qps capacity, which gives ~35% buffer over 220 qps and leaves room for autoscaling buffer.

Pre-cutover validation checklist (proposed):
1) Staging dry-run (full traffic mirror at 20% of production) — validate latency & error rates (target <0.5% errors).
2) Warm KV/prefix cache priming with synthetic traffic (48 hours) to reach steady-state cache hit rate.
3) Throughput ramp exercise: 0% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% of mirrored traffic with perf checks at each step.
4) Regression suite against golden prompts (quality check) and hallucination thresholds.
5) Smoke rollback procedure: immediate re-route to hosted API for any metrics breach.

Dry-run proposal: Apr 10 (Saturday) — run mirror at 20% for 6 hours, followed by a 2-hour escalation window; this gives us two weeks before the proposed cutover for fixes.

Cutover windows (final):
- Primary: Apr 24 (Sat) 02:00–06:00 PDT — capacity switch and live traffic ramp over 90 minutes.
- Backup: Apr 25 (Sun) 02:00–06:00 PDT.

Risks & mitigations: 
- Risk: initial cold cache penalty causing >P50 latency spikes. Mitigation: extended priming + staged ramp and short-circuiting large-batch requests to hosted endpoints for the first hour.
- Risk: token quota-related throttles. Mitigation: pre-cutover token cap increase and monitoring hooks in console.

Attachments: sizing-estimate.pdf (contains node-level cost delta and acceptance matrix).

Next steps: Ben — can you confirm procurement will accept a 3-node initial commit and share contract milestone dates? I'll prepare a short runbook and invite the ops/reliability owners (suggest: include eng-on-call and platform-ops).
